extracted.intended_audience: federal statisticians, statistical agency leadership, policymakers, and researchers interested in data ethics and official statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Systematic comparative analysis of alignment, tension, and gaps between the ASA Ethical Guidelines and U.S. guidance for official statistics (OMB SPD1/2/2a, NASEM PNP, OMB Data Ethics Tenets). Produces coded two-dimensional matrices and summaries of areas of support, tension, and guidance gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB SPD1 Responsibility 1: Produce and disseminate relevant and timely information
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce and disseminate relevant and timely information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPD1 articulates high-level expectations for federal statistical agencies; responsibility 1 emphasizes relevance and timeliness but may create tensions with other ethical expectations (e.g., accuracy, protection of data providers) when implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB SPD1 Responsibility 2: Conduct credible and accurate statistical activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct credible and accurate statistical activities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPD1 Responsibility 2 is aligned strongly with ASA EG principles supporting methodological rigor and credibility; considered a core goal for federal statistical agencies and a basis for possible elevation to regulation or law.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB SPD1 Responsibility 3: Conduct objective statistical activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct objective statistical activities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPD1 Responsibility 3 aligns with ASA EG elements that promote objectivity and lack of bias; alignment illustrated in coded tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB SPD1 Responsibility 4: Protect the trust of information providers by ensuring the confidentiality and exclusive statistical use of their responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect the trust of information providers by ensuring the confidentiality and exclusive statistical use of their responses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibility 4 concerns confidentiality and exclusive statistical use; the paper notes alignment with ASA EG Principle D but also identifies a guidance gap where SPD1 could include more practice-level behavioral guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 1.1 Survey planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey planning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of SPD2 Standards and Guidelines for Statistical Surveys describing expectations across the information collection lifecycle; survey planning supports evaluation of expected quality and burden of proposed information collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 1.2 Survey design
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey design
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey design standard under SPD2; intended to be broad to accommodate differing methods while supporting assessment of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 1.3 Survey response rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey response rates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard covering response rate considerations and related analyses required for OMB review under the Paperwork Reduction Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 1.4 Pretesting survey systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Pretesting survey systems
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation to pretest systems to evaluate functionality and reduce burden/measurement error prior to full deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 2.1 Developing sampling frames
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing sampling frames
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of collection of data standards; requires appropriate frame development to support representativeness and valid inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 2.2 Required notification of potential survey respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Required notification of potential survey respondents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard about informing potential respondents as part of ethical and legal information collection practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 2.3 Data collection methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Data collection methodology
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies expectations for method selection and implementation to support quality and minimize respondent burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 3.1 Data editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Data editing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for editing collected data to ensure accuracy and suitability for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 3.2 Nonresponse analysis and response rate calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonresponse analysis and response rate calculation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations for analyzing nonresponse and calculating response rates to assess potential biases and data quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 3.3 Coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Coding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for coding responses to ensure consistency and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 3.4 Data protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Data protection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements to protect data from unauthorized access and to preserve confidentiality throughout the lifecycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 3.5 Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations for periodic evaluation of data collection activities and quality assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 4.1 Developing estimates and projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing estimates and projections
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards addressing estimation, projection methods, and their appropriate use and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 5.1 Analysis and report planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis and report planning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on planning analyses and dissemination products to meet user needs and support interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 6.1 Review of information products
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of information products
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires review procedures to ensure quality, accuracy, and appropriateness of released products.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 7.1 Releasing information
rubrics_metrics.description: Releasing information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards governing how information products are released to the public, balancing transparency and protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 7.2 Data protection and disclosure avoidance for dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Data protection and disclosure avoidance for dissemination
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific expectations to prevent disclosure during dissemination, including use of disclosure-avoidance techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 7.3 Survey documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey documentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards requiring documentation of survey design, methods, and limitations to support reuse and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2 7.4 Documentation and release of public use microdata
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation and release of public use microdata
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for preparing public-use microdata, balancing usability with confidentiality protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a: Standards and Guidelines for Cognitive Interviews (Interview guide & A.1–A.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview guide and appendix items A.1 Methodological plan; A.2 Sample selection; A.4 Analysis of cognitive interviews; A.5 Transparent analysis; A.6 Final reports; A.7 Reporting results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPD2a provides standards for cognitive interviewing, including methodological planning, sample selection, transparent analysis, and reporting results. Used as an addendum to SPD2 to guide pretesting and questionnaire development.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Principle 1: Relevance to policy issues and society
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance to policy issues and society
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An aspirational goal for federal statistical agencies; intended to ensure statistics address important policy and societal questions, but achieving relevance can create tensions with other principles (e.g., privacy, mission limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Principle 2: Credibility among data users and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Credibility among data users and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle emphasizing methodological soundness and transparency to build credibility; strongly aligned with ASA EG elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Principle 3: Trust among the public and data providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust among the public and data providers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on preserving public trust through confidentiality, fairness, and respectful treatment of data providers; alignment with ASA EG Principle D noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Principle 4: Independence from political and other undue external influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence from political and other undue external influence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence is essential for objective statistics; ASA EG align with this principle to support unbiased production of statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Principle 5: Continual improvement and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Continual improvement and innovation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspirational principle encouraging research, staff development, and methodological advances; the paper notes potential guidance gaps in operationalizing this principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 1: A clearly defined and well accepted mission
rubrics_metrics.description: A clearly defined and well accepted mission
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice supports alignment with agency purpose and constrains collection/release of data to mission-appropriate activities; relevance tensions may arise when mission limits conflict with public interest requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 2: Necessary authority and procedures to protect independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary authority and procedures to protect independence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for legal/administrative authority and procedures that safeguard statistical independence; ASA EG elements support these protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 3: Commitment to quality and professional standards of practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitment to quality and professional standards of practice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes professional standards, training, and QA processes; strongly aligned with ASA EG.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 4: Professional advancement of staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional advancement of staff
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice encourages staff development and career progression; the analysis finds guidance gaps across some federal directives regarding staff advancement and active research programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 5: An active research program
rubrics_metrics.description: An active research program
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages agencies to maintain research programs to support methodological innovation; noted as a potential guidance gap in SPD documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 6: Strong internal and external evaluation processes for an agency’s statistical programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong internal and external evaluation processes for an agency’s statistical programs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports continuous improvement and accountability; ASA EG alignment is observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 7: Coordination and collaboration with other statistical agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordination and collaboration with other statistical agencies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While beneficial, unsafeguarded collaboration may create tensions with ASA EG elements (e.g., privacy, protecting vulnerable groups); implementation should balance collaboration with ethical protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 8: Respect for data providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect for data providers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for treating providers respectfully, maintaining confidentiality and minimizing burden; strongly supported by ASA EG Principle D elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 9: Dissemination of statistical products that meet users’ needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Dissemination of statistical products that meet users’ needs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on user-centered dissemination but may conflict with privacy/protection or ASA EG elements if not carefully balanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM Practice 10: Openness about sources and limitations of the data provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Openness about sources and limitations of the data provided
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about data provenance and limitations; ASA EG elements support this practice though some guidance gaps were noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet 1: Uphold applicable statutes, regulations, professional practices, and ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Uphold applicable statutes, regulations, professional practices, and ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tenet emphasizes legal and professional compliance; ASA EG fully supports this tenet.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet 2: Respect the public, individuals, and communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect the public, individuals, and communities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes respect and avoidance of harms to individuals and communities; ASA EG aligns strongly with this tenet.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet 3: Respect privacy and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect privacy and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on privacy/confidentiality protections; analysis identified a guidance gap where OMB DET could include more practice-level guidance similar to ASA EG.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet 4: Act with honesty, integrity, and humility
rubrics_metrics.description: Act with honesty, integrity, and humility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional conduct standard supported by ASA EG; identified as one of the tenets fully supported by all ASA EG principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet 5: Hold oneself and others accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold oneself and others accountable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accountability across data lifecycle; ASA EG supports accountability and professional responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet 6: Promote transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote transparency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency in data practices, sources, and limitations; ASA EG elements support this though some guidance gaps exist in practice-level detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet 7: Stay informed of developments in the fields of data management and data science
rubrics_metrics.description: Stay informed of developments in the fields of data management and data science
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations for continuous learning and staying current; analysis notes potential guidance gap where operational guidance could be strengthened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degrees of Freedom Analysis (DoFA) as an evaluation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Degrees of Freedom Analysis: a structured qualitative content-analysis approach used to identify patterns and themes in narrative guidance and to assess alignment across guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoFA assembles evidence into two-dimensional tables, searches for patterns of alignment/tension/gaps, does not require quantitation for two-dimensional alignment, and has been adapted for decision making and comparative guideline analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code assignment and double-coding consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed code assignment by primary coder followed by secondary coder evaluation and consensus discussions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First author applies detailed codes; second author reviews and any disagreements are discussed to reach consensus or flagged as requiring further clarity. Detailed coded tables are presented in annexes; summary tables are used for communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding convention: all coding in terms of ASA Ethical Guidelines (ASA EG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coding identifies ASA EG elements that align with, conflict with, or are absent relative to elements of the other guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alignment, tension, and conflicts are reported in terms of ASA EG elements; this centered-coding approach yields consistent signals across comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment scenario: literal or conceptual match
rubrics_metrics.description: Literal or conceptual match (alignment) between guideline elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is a thematic or exact match, the ASA EG element is indicated; example shows direct alignment between ASA EG D4 and OMB SPD1 Responsibility 4. Cells showing alignment are shaded green in the matrices and indicated by a check mark (✓).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment scenario: similar match (partial alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar match where alignment is abstract or holds under specific circumstances
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such matches are indicated with the ASA EG element in parentheses; represented visually and in coded tables as partial alignment (e.g., (⑇)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition (conflict)
rubrics_metrics.description: A guideline element that could potentially cause conflict with an ASA EG element
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicated by ASA EG element in red font with a '~' marker in the detailed coding; example: potential conflict between ASA EG D10 (provenance/fitness-for-use) and achieving NASEM PNP Principle 1 relevance when data unfit for purpose are considered relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tension (coexistence of alignment and conflict)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances where alignment and potential conflict coexist between guideline elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both ASA EG aligned and opposed elements are indicated in a cell; patterns with both alignment and tension are shaded yellow in the matrices and indicated by ✓ and ~ together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unmatched / Guidance gap
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances where a guideline element in one document has no corresponding element in the other document (guidance gap)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shown as a blank cell in detailed matrices and shaded gray for patterns; example: ASA EG Principle F offers no support for NASEM PNP Practice 9 dissemination of products that meet users' needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete alignment (pattern level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patterns of complete alignment across a row or column in the alignment matrices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple related cells show alignment, the pattern is shaded green and summarized as complete alignment in summary tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete tension (pattern level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patterns where alignment and conflict predominate across a row or column
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When both alignment and conflict are consistently present, the pattern is shaded yellow and summarized as complete tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visual/key indicators in coding matrices
rubrics_metrics.description: Key: ✓ indicates alignment, ~ indicates conflict, ✓ and ~ indicates tension, blank indicates unmatched; shading (green/yellow/gray) indicates pattern-level alignment/tension/gap
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper uses these visual conventions in Tables and Annexes to communicate findings succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment categories for comparative analysis: Areas of Strong Alignment, Areas of Tension, Guidance Gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary-level categories used to report comparative results between guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Areas of Strong Alignment identify where ASA EG fully supports other guidance; Areas of Tension highlight potential conflicts to be resolved before elevating guidance; Guidance Gaps identify where additional practice-level direction could improve implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience alignment consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration that guidance documents have differing intended audiences (e.g., SPD targeted to agency leadership vs OMB DET broader across agencies) and that audience differences affect interpretation and coding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The coding and interpretation take audience differences into account when assessing alignment, tension, or gaps; differences can explain why a practice appears absent or less detailed in one guidance compared to another.
